GENERATE BURST T1K-walk-r1 — (second attempt: attempt 1 lost the green plate in both variants) Run C-9 pipeline test T1 (Matt R-C9-61): PAINT-OVER of KEY FRAMES of the 3D knight's walk (his stride (key poses of him stepping forward)) in six directions, on one sheet. task_id "T1K-walk-r1".

IMAGE 1 is a SHEET of 12 key frames on flat pure #00ff00, a 4x3 grid, each frame centred in its own cell. The frames are renders of a 3D model of a knight carrying his POLLAXE upright in his right hand; their POSES, OUTLINES, POSITIONS and SIZES are correct, but their surface is flat, pale and plastic. The cells show him from different directions, in reading order:
row 1: facing the viewer (south), facing the viewer (south), facing away to the upper-right (north-east), facing away to the upper-right (north-east);
row 2: seen from behind (north), seen from behind (north), facing away to the upper-left (north-west), facing away to the upper-left (north-west);
row 3: facing the viewer's left (west), facing the viewer's left (west), facing the lower-left (south-west), facing the lower-left (south-west).
IMAGE 2 is the APPROVED painting of this same knight from six of those directions, a 3x2 grid: top row facing the viewer (south), lower-left (south-west), left (west); bottom row upper-left seen from behind (north-west), from behind (north), upper-right seen from behind (north-east). Use the matching view for each cell: his exact helm and visor, gorget, plate armour, the blue tabard with gold crosses and diagonal gold-and-blue bands on BOTH front and back, and the painter's hand (dark ink line, hatching, transparent washes). IMAGE 3 is the pollaxe itself (broadside and edge-on): its exact design.
Use image_gen in EDIT mode on IMAGE 1 and deliver ONE 1536x1024 sheet in which EVERY one of the 12 figures is repainted as the knight of IMAGE 2 seen from that cell's direction, in EXACTLY that frame's pose, outline, position and size (same place in its cell, same leg and arm angles, feet on the same spot, the pollaxe at the same place and angle with his gauntlet closed around the haft). All 12 must be ONE consistent knight in ONE consistent hand: the same armour, heraldry, helm, pollaxe and colours.
The tabard's RED LINING shows only as a narrow edge where the tabard's flaps part and at its hem, as in IMAGE 2: wherever IMAGE 1 shows large red areas on the tabard, paint them as the blue-and-gold tabard of IMAGE 2.
Keep the background flat pure #00ff00 and the 4x3 grid exactly as laid out: no frame added, removed, merged or reordered, no cell borders, no text, no ground shadows.

THE BACKGROUND IS A CHROMA-KEY PLATE, AND IT IS THE FIRST REQUIREMENT: every pixel outside the 12 figures must stay EXACTLY flat pure #00ff00, as it is in IMAGE 1 — no dark background, no gradient, no glow or light column behind the figures, no vignette, no shadow. A previous attempt replaced the green with a dark gradient and had to be thrown away. Before you copy the output, look at the corners and at the gaps between the figures: if they are not bright pure green, the image is wrong; regenerate it.
STYLE: the REGISTER CARD above is satisfied BY IMAGE 2: copy its hand; do not restyle.

Two image_gen EDIT calls: variants a and b. ONE retry per variant only if a frame's pose, facing or position changed, a frame is missing or duplicated, the knight differs between frames, the pollaxe moved or left his hand, or the background is not flat green — name the reason. Copy outputs to out/T1K-walk-r1_a.png and out/T1K-walk-r1_b.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "T1K-walk-r1"; images = the files with prompt, references (role + path) and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — the key-frame sheet to EDIT (12 walk keys of the Meshy 3D knight, six directions; poses correct, surface flat)
IMAGE 2 — the approved paintings of this knight from six directions (look, armour, heraldry, pollaxe, hand)
IMAGE 3 — the pollaxe's design (broadside and edge-on)
